summary: gRPC streaming: per-request idempotency header ends up in HTTP trailers and is dropped on reconnect causing duplicate tool/function invocations
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent duplicated function/tool invocations when using long-lived gRPC streams through our edge stack. Duplicates occur after transient connection loss and reconnect. Initial triage shows idempotency header (X-Idempotency-Key / x-redwood-idempotency) is present from client, but server processing path only sometimes observes it on replays.

Impact: SlateMaps sees duplicate downstream webhooks and doubled billing for about ~0.6% of streamed tool calls during heavy workload. Customer is on Dedicated capacity and uses our Go SDK in production. They have also reproduced locally with TS/Python clients.

Observed behavior: When the client sends per-message idempotency metadata for funcalls on a streamed session, an intermediate Envoy filter (custom header rewrite configured for legacy analytics) occasionally moves headers into HTTP/2/3 trailers (end_stream event). On reconnect + replay, the serving-runtime's replay path only checks initial request metadata for idempotency tokens — it does not look for trailer metadata, so some replays are treated as new requests and trigger duplicate tool invocations.
steps_to_reproduce: (Go) Start a streaming session with the Go SDK (grpc-go v1.56.0) against the customer's edge: set per-funcall metadata header 'x-redwood-idempotency' with unique UUID per tool invocation.
Simulate an edge-level transient connection drop (e.g., curl -X POST to our /simulate-failure endpoint or kill TCP connection on client), then let client reconnect and replay pending frames.
Observe server logs: sometimes the incoming request metadata on replay does not include 'x-redwood-idempotency' in initial headers, but it is present in HTTP/2 trailers (seen in pcap / envoy logs).
Repro with TS and Python SDKs by adding per-request idempotency metadata in the streamed message envelope rather than initial metadata; same duplicates observed when edge moves header to trailers.
logs: envoy (edge) trace: on StreamEnd header rewrite: move x-redwood-idempotency from header->trailer (filter: legacy-analytics-v1)
server (runtime) replay path: INFO replaying request id=abc123 initial-metadata={} (no x-redwood-idempotency)
server (runtime) exec: calling tool webhook idempotency-key=UNKNOWN -> POST /hooks/run (duplicate)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Arielle Chen (Support): Customer reported duplicates after a recent edge rewrite deployment. Assigned to Marco for runtime investigation.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Captured tcpdump; confirmed idempotency header present on client frames but arriving to runtime as HTTP trailer in ~12/50 repro attempts when envoy filter triggers. Suspect middleware moving headers on end_stream.

2026-03-11 14:20 - Devon Patel (Runtime Eng): Added a quick local patch to runtime replay path to fall back to trailers when header missing; reproduced dedupe fix locally. Preparing PR for review. Will coordinate canary deploy to staging.

2026-03-12 08:45 - SlateMaps (Customer): Confirmed repro with TS client in staging; duplicates stopped when they set idempotency key in initial-stream-metadata instead of per-message header. Asked for recommended SDK guidance and whether server can accept trailers permanently.

2026-03-13 10:30 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): PR merged for runtime to accept idempotency header from trailers for replays (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421). Drafting advisory to SDKs to add best-practice checks.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Support: Notifying customer of canary rollout schedule and recommended client mitigation (set idempotency at initial call metadata).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge filter rewrites analytic headers and moves them into trailers at end_stream; runtime only inspects initial metadata on replay. Evidence: envoy logs show header->trailer rewrite event coincident with duplicates.

Hypothesis 2: Some SDKs set per-message headers vs initial call metadata depending on helper utility patterns (Go/TS wrappers have historically allowed either). Customer code uses helper that attaches metadata per message. Repro across languages confirms this is client-agnostic; root cause is missing trailer handling in replay path.

Test: Added runtime fallback to inspect HTT P/2 trailers on replay. In staging this eliminated the dupes for the captured repro cases. Edge-case: trailers are only available on stream end; ensure fallback doesn't break streaming partial acks.
Telemetry: Instrumented counts for 'replay_without_initial_idempotency' and 'replay_with_trailer_idempotency' to measure incidence. Current rate ~0.6% in prod for this customer traffic shape.

Risk assessment: Accepting idempotency tokens from trailers is safe for replay (tokens are client-supplied). Need to ensure we normalize header casing and length; avoid accepting tokens from untrusted proxy modifications without auth checks.
resolution:
Mitigation steps: (1) Runtime patch merged to accept idempotency token from HTTP/2/3 trailers on replay path (PR #8421). (2) SDK guidance published: prefer setting per-call idempotency in initial stream metadata rather than per-message header; Go/TS/Python SDKs will include helper validation in next minor release to detect 'per-message header' usage and warn. (3) Customer advised to upgrade to runtime build with patch and to deploy SDK minor when available; temporary workaround: set idempotency token in initial metadata on connect.

Rollout notes: Canary deployed to staging 2026-03-12, canary to subset of us-east Dedicated on 2026-03-13 09:00, full prod rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 pending telemetry.

Follow-ups: (a) Add unit tests for trailer-handling in replay path. (b) Create an Envoy rule/guidance to avoid moving idempotency headers to trailers; coordinate with edge infra. (c) Add metrics alert if trailer-based idempotency hits >0.2% on customer traffic.
